memos.headline: CAT and AAPL Lead at 52-Week Highs While PG and AMZN Show Persistent Relative Weakness
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of today. CAT is printing a new 52-week high with RSI at 80.9 and +17.7% over four weeks — this is parabolic momentum that demands respect but also caution, as the extension above the 50d mean (+13.9%) and 200d mean (+33.0%) is extreme. AAPL and GOOGL are similarly strong with 12-week relative strength vs SPY of +14.5% and +31.2% respectively, both well above their moving averages and near highs, though AAPL's RSI at 71 is approaching overbought. On the weak side, PG is in a clear downtrend — below both its 50d and 200d means, RSI at 39.1, down 15.3% from its high, and showing -10.9% relative weakness vs SPY over 12 weeks. AMZN is similarly deteriorating with RSI 41.6, -9.3% drawdown, and -8.9% relative underperformance over four weeks, suggesting sellers are in control until price reclaims its 50d mean.

views.note: New 52-week high with massive momentum (+51% over 26w, +14.3% rel strength 4w), but RSI 80.9 is dangerously overbought — I'd trail stops tight and reassess on a close below 465 (roughly the 50d mean area).
Only 0.4% from 52-week high, strong uptrend above both moving averages with +14.5% 12w relative strength vs SPY; would turn neutral on a close below 233 (near the 50d mean).
Exceptional 12-week relative strength of +31.2% vs SPY, +38.1% 12w return, RSI 64 still has room — the strongest trend-on-trend setup in the universe; risk level is ~221 (50d mean area).
Near highs with RSI 63 and +71.1% 26w return, positive relative strength on all timeframes; high ATR (2.96%) means wider stops needed, would reassess below 178 (50d mean zone).
Persistent downtrend: below 50d and 200d means, RSI 39.1, -15.3% drawdown, and -10.9% 12w relative weakness vs SPY — no reason to step in front of this until price reclaims 155.
Below 50d mean, RSI 41.6, -9.3% drawdown, and -8.9% 4w relative weakness vs SPY indicate distribution; needs to reclaim 226 (50d area) to neutralize the bearish setup.
Sitting right at its 50d mean (+0.9%), RSI 56 is mid-range, and 12w relative strength vs SPY is -3.8% — no edge either way; would get interested on a breakout above 535 or a pullback to the 200d.
Violent +17.2% extension above 50d mean on a bear-market rally (still -42.4% from highs and below 200d mean); this is a counter-trend bounce, not a new uptrend — too risky to chase.
Healthy uptrend above both averages with RSI 55, but 12w relative strength vs SPY is flat at +0.6% — an in-line performer with no compelling edge right now.
Negative 12w and 26w returns, -8.4% 12w relative weakness vs SPY, and -9.7% drawdown from highs; trend is flat-to-down and I see no catalyst in the tape to get involved above 117.

memos.headline: NVDA and MSFT Lead on Earnings Power; JPM, XOM, and UNH Face Cash-Flow Compression
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in NVDA (+55.6% YoY revenue, 56.5% net margin) and MSFT (+18.1% YoY revenue, 35.6% net margin with net income up 23.6%), both demonstrating operating leverage at scale. AMZN's margin expansion to 10.8% with net income up 34.7% YoY on $167.7B revenue is encouraging, though I want to see that margin trajectory sustained before gaining full conviction. On the other side, JPM (-10.5% revenue, -17.4% net income YoY), XOM (-12.4% revenue, -23.4% net income), and UNH (+12.9% revenue but -19.2% net income with a razor-thin 3.1% margin) all show earnings compression that makes me uncomfortable paying up. CAT's flat revenue and -18.7% net income decline alongside $31.7B in debt signals late-cycle pressure I'd rather avoid.

views.note: 56.5% net margin and 55.6% YoY revenue growth on $46.7B quarterly revenue is extraordinary earnings power with minimal leverage ($8.5B debt).
18.1% YoY revenue growth to $76.4B with 35.6% net margin and 23.6% net income growth demonstrates durable, high-quality compounding.
Net income up 34.7% YoY with margin expanding to 10.8% on $167.7B revenue is promising, but I need sustained margin improvement to raise conviction.
29.2% net margin on $96.4B revenue with 13.8% top-line growth and low $14.8B debt is a clean earnings profile; a deceleration in ad revenue would change my view.
9.6% revenue growth and 24.9% margin are solid but not exceptional, and $91.8B in total debt is the highest in the tech cohort; Services mix shift would move me more constructive.
Only 1.7% revenue growth on $20.9B is barely above inflation, though 15.3% net income growth and 17.3% margin show cost discipline; organic volume acceleration would upgrade my view.
Revenue down 10.5% and net income down 17.4% YoY represent clear earnings compression; I'd need a revenue stabilization quarter to reconsider.
Revenue -12.4% and net income -23.4% YoY with an 8.7% margin on $81.5B revenue reflects commodity headwinds compressing cash flow.
Net income fell 19.2% YoY despite 12.9% revenue growth, leaving a 3.1% net margin on $111.6B revenue—cost pressures are overwhelming top-line gains.
Flat revenue (-0.7%) and -18.7% net income decline with $31.7B debt suggest late-cycle margin erosion; order book recovery would change my stance.

memos.headline: Fed in Easing Mode with Sticky Inflation: Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth, Neutral Banks
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime — the upper bound has dropped 75bp over the past year to 4.25%, with a 25bp cut in the last three months alone, while the 10y yield has fallen 22bp over three months to 4.13%. The yield curve has re-steepened meaningfully, with the 10y-2y spread at +55bp, up 39bp year-over-year, which historically supports banks but also signals the market pricing in slower growth ahead. CPI is running at 2.9% y/y, still above target, and the labor market is stable with unemployment flat at 4.3% over three months — this is a soft-landing setup, not a recession call. I have moderate conviction in duration-sensitive growth names (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN) as lower rates support valuations, but I'd be cautious on pure cyclicals like CAT given the growth deceleration signal from the curve. A September CPI print above 3.0% y/y or a sharp unemployment spike above 4.5% would force me to revisit this regime call.

views.note: Easing cycle and falling 10y yields directly support long-duration growth equities with strong recurring revenue.
Lower rates reduce discount rates on future cash flows; stable labor market supports consumer spending on premium hardware.
Duration-sensitive growth benefits from rate cuts, though elevated CPI could slow the pace of further easing, capping upside.
Easing cycle supports both the growth multiple and consumer discretionary spending with unemployment stable at 4.3%.
Steeper curve (+55bp 10y-2y) helps net interest margins, but further rate cuts compress short-end lending yields — offsetting forces.
Staples are a defensive hold; stable unemployment supports demand but 2.9% CPI pressures input costs and rate cuts reduce relative appeal.
Curve steepening driven by easing rather than growth optimism suggests cyclical deceleration risk; I'd wait for harder data confirmation.
Energy is more commodity-driven than rate-driven; slowdown signals from the curve are a mild headwind but not enough for a strong call.
Ad-driven revenue benefits from stable employment and consumer spending; falling yields support the growth multiple.
Healthcare is relatively rate-insensitive; stable macro backdrop is benign but no strong macro catalyst either way.

memos.headline: Limited Sentiment Signal Across Mega-Caps; NVDA Earnings Fade Already Priced, UNH Reg-FD Cluster Warrants Monitoring
memos.body: I see very little actionable sentiment differentiation across the universe this week. NVDA reported earnings on 8/27 and the stock barely moved (–0.8% next-day close), suggesting the narrative around AI capex is fully absorbed and crowded positive tone offers no edge. UNH stands out with three Reg-FD filings in rapid succession (8/20, 9/8, 9/9 amendment), which often signals management proactively shaping the narrative—worth watching for a tone inflection but I lack GDELT volume data to confirm direction. CAT's new material debt agreement on 9/3 and MSFT's board-level officer change on 9/30 are routine corporate housekeeping with no discernible sentiment shift. Overall, I have low conviction across the board given the thin evidence set and would wait for clearer tone-direction signals before taking positions.

views.note: Earnings reaction of only –0.8% indicates crowded positive sentiment already priced; no incremental edge from tone.
Cluster of three Reg-FD filings in three weeks hints at proactive narrative management, but direction of tone shift is unclear without GDELT data.
New debt obligation filing is routine; no evidence of a sentiment narrative shift around infrastructure or macro demand.
Two 'Other Events' 8-Ks in early September provide no clear tone signal; insufficient to form a directional view.
Board officer change on 9/30 is standard governance; no sentiment inflection detected.
Bylaw amendment filing is procedural with no media tone implications.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Elevated but Easing Near-Term; Weak Oil Signals Demand Concern More Than Supply Disruption
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index sits at 438.91, down 10.1% over the past month but still up 16.7% over three months, suggesting a structurally elevated policy backdrop even as the acute spike fades. VIX at 16.63 and HY OAS at 2.81% are both benign, indicating markets are not pricing imminent geopolitical disruption. WTI crude at $61.28 is down nearly 11% over three months, which I read as a demand-side signal rather than a supply-security premium—this argues against energy supply-chain stress but raises questions about global growth expectations that matter for industrials and tech capex. I have moderate conviction that the current environment favors domestically oriented names and those less exposed to export-control escalation, while names with heavy China hardware exposure (NVDA, AAPL) carry latent policy risk that the market is under-pricing given the still-elevated uncertainty index. A reversal in oil toward $70+ or a fresh round of semiconductor export controls would change my stance materially.

views.note: Structurally elevated policy uncertainty (+16.7% 3m) keeps semiconductor export-control risk alive; any tightening of China AI-chip rules would hit NVDA disproportionately.
China supply-chain concentration remains a latent risk under elevated policy uncertainty, but benign VIX and credit spreads suggest no imminent disruption.
WTI at $61.28 and falling 10.7% over 3 months reflects demand weakness rather than geopolitical supply premium; no energy-security bid visible.
Recent 8-K filing and weak oil/commodity backdrop suggest muted global capex cycle; policy uncertainty weighs on infrastructure spending visibility.
Primarily domestic ad revenue base and limited hardware export-control exposure make GOOGL a relative safe harbor amid elevated policy uncertainty.
Domestic healthcare demand is insulated from trade/geopolitical shocks; multiple Reg FD filings suggest active investor engagement, and benign credit conditions support the balance sheet.

Technical, fundamental, macro, and geopolitical analysts all lean long.
